title: Consistent embedding variant catalog: onboarding, compatibility, and sunsetting protocol
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable, low-risk process and runtime support for onboarding new embedding model variants and deprecating old ones without breaking customer indexes or reranking pipelines. Scope includes: (1) a canonical variant catalog and semantic versioning convention for embedding families, (2) runtime compatibility checks and automatic fallback rules in the reranker/embeddings endpoint, (3) migration playbooks for reindexing when embeddings change dimensionality, and (4) telemetry/eval gates for rollout (quality, latency, inference cost).

Requirements and decisions made so far:
- Variant naming: <family>-v<major>.<minor> (e.g., red-embed-v2.0). Major increments imply potential dimensionality or normalization changes; minor implies performance/quantization/throughput-only changes and should be compatible.
- Backwards compatibility: endpoint must accept explicit model parameter or a catalog alias (e.g., "recommended-embeddings") which maps to a stable variant. When a new major variant is introduced, we will not automatically switch aliases.
- Dimensionality changes: if a new major version changes vector dimension, index incompatibility is possible. We'll expose a migration endpoint and a reindex job template. Customers get an opt-in reindex with dry-run metrics (delta recall/precision) and estimated compute cost.
- Rollout policy: staged rollout by customer cohort: internal canary (0-2% traffic), beta accounts (3-10%), broader gradual ramp (10 -> 50 -> 100) with automated quality/latency gates at each step. Gate thresholds defined in evals (see telemetry).
- Fallback & graceful degradation: if quality regressions detected or latency/cost exceed thresholds, system automatically re-routes to pinned older variant for affected keys/tenant prefixes for up to 24 hours and creates a rollback alert.
- Console & API changes: add per-tenant model pinning, per-route variant override, and a "reindex recommended" flag in the Console index detail view.
- Telemetry: collect per-tenant embedding drift metrics (cosine similarity distribution vs baseline), downstream reranker impact (nDCG@10 on internal eval set), and per-token latency/cost.
- Security/compliance: embedding variants are code-free artifacts; however, Private deployments must support local model mapping. We will add a security_review_required flag for major family additions.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: implementing auto-rewrite of customer indices; connectors for 3rd-party vector stores (we provide templates but not direct force reindexing).

Artifacts and references:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embedding+Variant+Catalog+Design
- Migration runbook draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/embeddings/migration-runbook
- Prototype PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2481
- Telemetry dashboards (internal): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/embeddings-rollout

Success criteria:
- New variant can be onboarded and mapped to an alias without customer downtime.
- Rollout gates reliably detect a 3% drop in nDCG@10 or a 20% regression in p50 latency and automatically safe-fall to the pinned variant.
- Customers can request and run a dry-run reindex job and see cost + quality delta estimates before committing.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: customers with large indices (billions of vectors) cannot reindex quickly. Mitigation: provide an "incremental reindex" template and a recommended timeline/schedule plus partner-run service offering.
- Risk: dimension changes silently break downstream consumers. Mitigation: require explicit major version adoption and expose compatibility checks in the SDK that throw a clear error when dimension mismatches occur.
- Risk: rollout gates generate false positives from noisy metric windows. Mitigation: use robust statistics (rolling median, bootstrap CI) and require consecutive window failures (3 windows) before triggering automatic rollback.
